values.quote1: Footnote 1: "Energy density factors are based on the lower heating values of fuels in CA-GREET3.0" "using BTU to MJ conversion of 1055.06 J/Btu." (read 1, Justia; the tool split the sentence into two quotes)
values.quote2: Body: "Fuel quantities denominated in other units, such as those shown in Table 4, are converted to MJ in the LRT-CBTS" "by multiplying by the corresponding energy density" [footnote 1]; footnote 1: "Energy density factors are based on the lower heating values of fuels in CA-GREET3.0" "using BTU to MJ conversion of 1055.06 J/Btu." (read 2, Justia)
values.notes: Third read (Cornell LII, 17 CCR 95486): same footnote, names CA-GREET3.0. What is STATED: LCFS energy densities are LHV values from CA-GREET3.0. What FOLLOWS (not a separate sentence): LCFS carbon intensities are gCO2e per MJ of fuel energy (2025 FRO §95481: 'Carbon Intensity (CI)' means the quantity of life cycle greenhouse gas emissions, per unit of fuel energy,' [verbatim, one read; the tool paraphrased the rest as 'expressed in gCO2e/MJ']) and the regulation multiplies CI by MJ computed from these LHV energy densities, so the CA-GREET3.0 CIs in round 1 (cagreet3_lut2018.*) are per MJ LHV. No CA-GREET3.0 TSD/LUT sentence saying 'LHV' was found (round 1 and CA-GREET4.0 LUT TSD Aug 2024 both checked: no LHV/HHV mention). §95481 (2025 FRO) defines both 'Lower Heating Value (LHV)' ('... excluding the heat of condensation for water vapor produced during combustion') and 'Higher Heating Value (HHV)' ('... including ...'). Version caveat as for carb_lcfs.energy_density.*: the 2025 text (CA-GREET4.0) was not reachable.

rejected.reason: NETL 'Cradle-to-Gate Life Cycle Analysis Baseline for United States Coal Mining and Delivery', DOE/NETL-2024/4846, cover date December 20, 2023. This is the right source (US, mining + cleaning + transport, functional unit 'The functional unit for this LCA is 1 kg of coal delivered to a power plant.' Section 2.1 p. 8; Exhibit ES-2 title 'Global warming potential (AR6, 100-yr) impacts for all basin-coal type scenarios'), but two reads found NO absolute GWP value in text or tables: results are only in charts (Exhibits ES-2, 4-3, 4-7, 4-8); Exhibit 4-5 (p. 31) gives each scenario only as a percent of the production-weighted U.S. average (e.g. PRB-S 39%, IB-B 131%, SA-B 460%); Appendix C TRACI summary tables (Exhibits C-1 to C-3) are not in the extracted text. Heating values (Exhibit 3-2, p. 16, Btu/lb, HHV/LHV not stated): U.S. bituminous 1.20E+04, subbituminous 8.76E+03, lignite 6.62E+03. Next step: stage the PDF (incl. Appendix C) or the EDX dataset files.

EDX dataset 'LCA Baseline for U.S. Coal Mining and Delivery Data Products' (Cutshaw et al., 3/25/2025, DOI 10.18141/2560300, CC0) holds only an openLCA model (netl_coal_delivery_lca_baseline_model_v4_12262024.zolca, 30.5 MB) and Basin-CoalType-MineTypeInventories.xlsx (1.76 MB); no printed result; previews need an EDX account. Binary -> files to stage, not a transcription.

US coal inputs printed are only mine methane factors (8 scf/ton PRB surface, 360 scf/ton Illinois No. 6 underground; Exhibit 5-12 p. 19), not intensities -> rejected.

Columbia SIPA student capstone 'Upstream Emissions of Coal and Gas' (Scull et al., April 28, 2017, rev. May 24, 2017): the report's own weighting of reviewed studies, stated on a 20-YEAR GWP basis; not a government or primary LCA source; single read -> rejected.

Same as prod_through_distribution.ar5: no readable AR5 figure (Appendix E spreadsheet not readable via WebFetch; round 1 also tried the EDX appendix page).

2025 LCFS Final Regulation Order (unofficial, OAL-approved 27 June 2025, operative 1 July 2025; 07012025 and 08112025 PDFs): WebFetch text (~110k chars) stops in §95483 and never reaches §95486 Table 4 (table of contents: 'Table 4. Energy Densities and Conversion Factors for LCFS Fuels and Blendstocks', p. 80). The 2026-10 proposed amendments (Appendix A-4) text also omits Table 4. So the registered values come from the CCR text as last amended 1-4-2019 (Justia/Cornell); whether 2025 changed Table 4 or its 'CA-GREET3.0' footnote is unverified.

CARB 'Technical Support Documentation for Lookup Table Pathways Proposed Amendments for the LCFS Regulation' (Aug 12, 2024; CA-GREET4.0): one read; no 'LHV'/'HHV'/'lower heating value' in the text; only 'The energy flow rates of gaseous and solid streams are calculated using their heating values.' No energy density table.

gaps: Coal upstream (mining + transport) for US power-plant coal: still no free source with a printed US average as text. The best source exists but prints results only in charts: NETL DOE/NETL-2024/4846 (Dec 2023; AR6 100-yr; per kg coal delivered to a power plant). Files to stage: the OSTI PDF (https://www.osti.gov/servlets/purl/2370100/) for pdftotext of Appendix C Exhibits C-1..C-3 if present, or EDX dataset DOI 10.18141/2560300 (Basin-CoalType-MineTypeInventories.xlsx; openLCA model). Until then the 3B/3C-up/3D-up coal term stays held/partial, never zero.

Oil-fired generation upstream (residual fuel oil, distillate at power plants): no free readable source found in this round (no NETL/GREET/CARB/EPA printed value located). CA-GREET3.0 ULSD WTT (round 1) is the only distillate proxy and is a California pathway on an unstated (per this round: LHV, via LCFS Table 4) basis; nothing for residual fuel oil.
NETL AR5 natural gas values: still not obtained (Appendix E spreadsheet). Register 7.8/8.8 as AR6 with explicit gwp_set and disclose, or stage Appendix E.
LCFS Table 4 currency: values are the CCR text last amended 1-4-2019 (footnote cites CA-GREET3.0). Confirm against the 2025 FRO (CA-GREET4.0) by staging its PDF before registering.

CA-GREET3.0 LHV basis is now STATED for LCFS energy densities (Table 4 footnote 1) and carries to LCFS gCO2e/MJ by the credit formula; no CA-GREET TSD sentence says 'LHV' directly. Converting round-1 CA-GREET g/MJ (LHV) to per-gallon or HHV-MMBtu terms should use the LCFS Table 4 MJ/gal values (LHV), not Hub HHV heat contents.
LCFS CNG row is per THERM (105.5 MJ/Therm = 100,000 Btu x 1055.06 J/Btu), not per scf; a therm is normally an HHV billing unit although the footnote says LHV. Do not use it to convert scf.
